solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Paintings sale row — court involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these words are mixed together

explanation.surface: An auction of pictures descends into a row that ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' tells you to scramble the twelve letters of SALE ROW and COURT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures painted in water-based pigments are a common kind of painting, named after the medium.

clue.text: Visible from Veronica's settee, container for recording

indicators.note: Visible from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something can be seen from Veronica's sofa: a box for keeping recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cassette is a small plastic case holding magnetic tape for audio or video recordings.

clue.text: Clergyman's article located in study

definitions.note: read as 'Clergyman is', the noun defining the answer

indicators.note: located in says the article is placed inside the room word

parts.note: a den is a private room for study or work
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A churchman's essay can be found in his study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clergyman's' stands for 'Clergyman is'; 'article' looks like a piece of writing but is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior cleric in charge of a cathedral or chapter holds this title, so it names a clergyman.

clue.text: Information on girl in Swiss city

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information
Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone has details about a girl living in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal British phrase 'get the gen' means get the facts; 'on' in a down clue puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on Lake Leman in western Switzerland is home to many international bodies.

clue.text: Middle Easterner seen — able, flexible

indicators.note: flexible means able to bend into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A person from the Middle East is observed to be capable and adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' asks for the letters of SEEN and ABLE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Lebanon, a country on the eastern Mediterranean, is a native of the Middle East.

clue.text: Monsieur with help, servant

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, French for Mr
aid means help

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with assistance gets a domestic worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic employee, especially a female one doing housework, is a kind of servant.

clue.text: A daughter taking long time to see truism

parts.note: an age is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: A daughter takes ages to recognise an obvious truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A saying is a traditional statement of supposed general truth, close in sense to a truism.

clue.text: Half of scheme ignored by artist — extremely lurid colour

indicators.note: Half of points to three of the six letters in the word scheme
ignored says the first half is dropped, so the second half is kept

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: extremely means the two end letters of the word lurid are taken

explanation.surface: An artist drops half of a garish design, leaving it in a vivid colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of scheme ignored' drops the first half, keeping EME; 'extremely' takes L and D, the ends of 'lurid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright green shade named after the precious gemstone is a colour.

clue.text: Potential heir ends date with lower expectations?

indicators.note: Potential means what something could become, so these letters may be formed into another word

explanation.surface: A would-be heir ends a date feeling less hopeful about what's coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' signals rearranging HEIR ENDS DATE. The question mark flags the playful definition: having lost heart, you expect less.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost heart or spirit feels discouraged and so expects less from the future.

clue.text: Main feature of German city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr region of Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A German city's chief attraction is its church.
explanation.definitionFit: The core quality or most important part of something is its fundamental nature or heart.

clue.text: Aides with name for island mountains

indicators.note: with joins the word Aides to the swap that follows
N for I means one letter takes the place of the other

explanation.surface: Assistants swap a name for an island when planning a trip to the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: In AIDES, the I (island) is replaced by N (name).
explanation.definitionFit: The long South American range running down the continent's western side is a chain of mountains.

clue.text: Catty set I abandoned in Rome once

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A spiteful group is left behind in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like 'left behind' but signals rearranging CATTY SET I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Rome was an independent city governing its own territory, an example of a self-governing urban state.

clue.text: Buildings expert certain to include volume Roy brought up

indicators.note: to include means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word Roy is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A building inspector is sure to include the volume that Roy mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' works as a reversal because this is a down entry, read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who inspects and values property and buildings is called this, so is a buildings expert.

clue.text: It's nailed low down

parts.note: a digit at the bottom of the foot has a nail on it; 'nailed' suggests carpentry or capture

explanation.surface: Something has been hammered in near the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nailed' suggests fixed with nails, but it means bearing a toenail; 'low down' places it at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Each digit of the foot carries a nail and sits at the very bottom of the body.

clue.text: Not drinking alcohol, Peg to speak briefly

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: talk means speak

explanation.surface: A teetotaller called Peg wants to say a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a name but is a golf tee; 'briefly' trims TALK to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcoholic drinks is described this way.

clue.text: Shelter wrapped in fleece

indicators.note: wrapped in says the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Finding protection by bundling up in a woolly jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: The side sheltered from the wind is the sheltered side, so the word means protection or shelter.

clue.text: One profiting illegally from tennis equipment and beers uncovered

parts.note: a racket is used to hit the ball in tennis

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of beers are stripped away

explanation.surface: A crook makes money from tennis gear and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the first and last letters from 'beers', leaving EER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs a dishonest or fraudulent scheme for money is a gangster-style criminal operator.

clue.text: Exclamation of admiration about fine English stove

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the pieces that follow

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise or admiration
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Someone admires a fine English stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is the British slang 'cor!', roughly 'wow!'; 'about' wraps it around the next two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance with hob and oven for preparing food is a stove.

clue.text: Some fun duenna finds excessive

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chaperone thinks a certain amount of fun is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link word; a duenna is an older woman chaperoning girls in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwarranted or more than is appropriate is excessive.

clue.text: Starts to drizzle awfully, new kit wet

indicators.note: Starts to means the first letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: As drizzle begins, new kit gets terribly wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasantly damp and cold, like a cellar, is a sense of wet.

clue.text: Expose firm; note result

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A whistleblower reveals a company and writes down the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: The way things turn out, the consequence of an action, is its result.

clue.text: Friar's sweets for schoolchildren

definitions.meaning: the name of Robin Hood's jolly friar
British school slang for food, especially snacks and sweets

explanation.surface: A monk hands out treats to pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion; in British boarding-school slang the same word means snacks and sweets.

clue.text: US city jeans so fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imagined, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An American city's denim is very stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective about jeans but signals rearranging JEANS SO.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Californian city at the heart of Silicon Valley is a place in the United States.

clue.text: Hundred have high opinion of old car

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: A hundred people rate an old banger.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a battered old motor vehicle, like a box on wheels.
